data.title: Cidofovir (systemic + topical/intralesional)
data.summary: Antivirals & ART · Acyclic nucleoside phosphonate (cytosine nucleotide analogue)
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Antivirals & ART_

**Class:** Acyclic nucleoside phosphonate (cytosine nucleotide analogue)

## Mechanism of action
- Already carries a phosphonate group, so needs only host kinases (no viral TK) → cidofovir diphosphate inhibits viral DNA polymerase
- Broad DNA virus activity: CMV, HSV (including acyclovir-resistant), VZV, HPV, poxviruses (molluscum, orf), adenovirus
- Very long intracellular half-life → weekly/fortnightly dosing

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- IV: CMV retinitis in AIDS; acyclovir- and foscarnet-resistant HSV
- Topical 1–3% (compounded gel/cream): acyclovir-resistant HSV ulcers, recalcitrant warts (anogenital, periungual) and molluscum in immunocompromised patients (HIV, transplant), recurrent respiratory papillomatosis
- Intralesional: recalcitrant warts (case series)

## Dose & formulations
- IV: 5 mg/kg once weekly × 2, then every 2 weeks — always with probenecid (2 g 3 h before, 1 g at 2 and 8 h after) and 1 L normal saline
- Topical 1–3% once daily, 5 days a week, for several cycles

## Adverse effects
- IV: dose-limiting nephrotoxicity (proximal tubule — Fanconi syndrome), neutropenia, ocular hypotony/uveitis, metabolic acidosis
- Topical: local erosion, ulceration, burning (inflammation is common); absorption from large areas can cause renal toxicity

## Contraindications
- Renal impairment (creatinine >1.5 mg/dL or proteinuria), concurrent nephrotoxic drugs, probenecid/sulfa allergy (for IV)
- Pregnancy

## Drug interactions
- Nephrotoxic drugs (aminoglycosides, amphotericin B, foscarnet, NSAIDs, tenofovir)

## Monitoring
- Creatinine and urine protein before each IV dose; CBC; eye exams

## Pregnancy & lactation
Avoid (carcinogenic/teratogenic in animals).

## Viva points
- Nucleotide analogue — TK-independent
- Topical cidofovir for warts/molluscum in HIV and acyclovir-resistant HSV
- IV always with probenecid and saline (nephrotoxicity)

_Sources: Khopkar ch.3 and ch.20 (Cidofovir); Wolverton 4e ch.11 and ch.43. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
